# References {.unnumbered}

## Book sources (Zinux repository, `docs/`)

- `README.md` — AI-native driver model, snapshots, VSL overview, 1.0 gate
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — hybrid microkernel, memory model, IPC, drivers, build
- `DOCUMENTATION.md` — over-documentation standard
- `ROADMAP_EN.md` — Phases 0–37 with files and tests
- `1.0.md` — machine-checked 1.0 requirements
- `AGENTS.md` — research principles (the method behind this book)
- `PLUGIN_MODEL.md`, `PLUGIN_SIGNING.md`, `PLUGIN_AUDIT.md`
- `VSL_SPEC.md` — Väinö Subsystem for Linux
- `UART.md` — the UART driver experiment (860-line research spec)
- `HW_CAP_PROTOCOL.md`, `NO_DRIVERS.md`, `SELF_HEAL.md`, `FEDERATION.md`, `EEDEN.md`
- `REAL_HARDWARE.md` — HP Stream USB-boot guide

## Prior art and inspiration

- Ryzhyk et al., *User-Guided Device Driver Synthesis*, OSDI 2014 (Termite / Termite-2)
- seL4 microkernel — capability model
- Limine boot protocol — <https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine>
- OSDev Wiki — <https://wiki.osdev.org/>
- Zig Language Reference — <https://ziglang.org/documentation/master/>
- Graphene Kernel — Zig hybrid microkernel experiment

## Book infrastructure

- Quarto publishing system — <https://quarto.org/>
- Structure adapted from Pedro Duarte Faria, *Introduction to Zig: a project-based book* ([zig-book](https://github.com/pedropark99/zig-book), CC-BY 4.0; Finnish fork [zig-book-FI](https://mikko-huuskonen-pro.github.io/zig-book-FI/))
